verdict.rationale: Notte documents programmatic, non-interactive operation. Cloud browser sessions are controlled via an authenticated API, the CLI drives browsers through shell commands, and scripts deploy as serverless endpoints that can be invoked and scheduled anywhere. Together these cover headless automation. missing for 10: explicit CI-pipeline documentation (e.g. GitHub Actions or other CI runner examples), independent or hands-on corroboration of headless/CI usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Sessions are isolated browser instances running in the cloud that you can control programmatically.
The Notte CLI lets AI agents control browsers through simple shell commands.
Serverless automations you can invoke and schedule anywhere.
All API requests require a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header.
